In the case of SiC, PowerAmerica supported a vibrant U.S. SiC fab infrastructure that not only stopped the bleeding of domestic semiconductor chip manufacturing from going overseas, but also brought multiple Asian and European companies to manufacture chips in the U.S. The competitive system advantages of both SiC and GaN were amply demonstrated in over 100 projects, which contributed to high demand with economies-of-scale price reductions. SiC and GaN are close to cost parity in PV systems, and that is increasingly becoming the case with other volume power applications. As early as 2020, we met our metric of SiC chip pricing below $0.10/A. TECHNOLOGY ADVANCEMENT Significant WBG technology advancements were made through the 212 industry, university, and National Lab projects carried out. We established the world’s first SiC foundry in X-FAB Texas; the insertion of SiC at Microchip with the world’s first 3.3 kV MOSFET in production; and performed 3.3 kV, 6.5 kV, and 10 kV MOSFET projects at Wolfspeed. The X-FAB foundry made it possible for many U.S. SiC fabless companies — which would have otherwise gone overseas — to manufacture chips domestically. These companies include General Electric (GE), Coherent, Qorvo, SemiQ, GeneSiC (now part of Navitas), Littelefuse, and Alpha & Omega Semiconductor. In addition, we supported the development of IP at design houses like Sonrisa, NC State University, and SUNY — which then licensed the fabrication processes they developed at X-FAB to give SiC newcomers quick access to production and markets. WBG chips require specialized modules capable of high voltage, high current, high temperature, and high frequency. We developed reliable and rugged modules through our projects at GE and Wolfspeed. PowerAmerica’s $140M in those 212 power SiC and GaN projects addressed chip design, fabrication, testing, modules, reliability, ruggedness, and all major applications — including automotive and rail traction, on-board chargers, photovoltaic, consumer electronics, aerospace, flexible alternating current transmission systems (FACTS), high-voltage DC systems (HVDC), microgrids, energy storage, wind power, motor drives, UPS, and data centers. Execution of these seed projects demonstrated SiC and GaN’s respective competitive advantages.
